record.original_question: Let A={a_1<a_2<...}⊆N have positive asymptotic density d, so that n/a_n→d. Does there always exist a subset B={b_1<b_2<...}⊆A with positive asymptotic density d_0, where 0<d_0≤d, such that n/b_n converges to d_0 more rapidly than n/a_n converges to d? Equivalently, can one find such a B and a function f(n)→0 with b_n=n/d_0(1+o(f(n)))? In particular, can this be done with f(n)=1/log n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be a set of positive integers with positive asymptotic density $d$, meaning $\lim_{n\to\infty} n/a_n = d \in (0,1]$.

(a) Does there always exist a subset $B=\{b_1<b_2<\cdots\}\subseteq A$ having positive asymptotic density $d_0$ with $0<d_0\le d$, such that the convergence $n/b_n\to d_0$ is faster than the convergence $n/a_n\to d$? Equivalently, do there exist such a $B$ and a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to(0,\infty)$ with $f(n)\to 0$ for which
$$b_n=\frac{n}{d_0}\bigl(1+o(f(n))\bigr)\qquad(n\to\infty)?$$

(b) In particular, can this be achieved with the explicit rate $f(n)=1/\log n$, i.e. can one always find $B\subseteq A$ of positive asymptotic density $d_0\in(0,d]$ with
$$b_n=\frac{n}{d_0}\Bigl(1+o\!\left(\tfrac{1}{\log n}\right)\Bigr)?$$

Either prove that such a subset $B$ always exists, or exhibit a set $A$ of positive asymptotic density for which no such $B$ exists.

Related work on uniform/Banach density and on densities of subsets by Grekos and collaborators exists, but no specific source confirming the problem as solved (in either direction, including the case $f(n)=1/\log n$) was identified.
